content.title: About
content.content: Caramel dip (regular) is a thick sweet sauce made from sugar, butter and cream, often flavored with vanilla. It is perfect for drizzling over ice cream, desserts, pancakes and fruit. The product has a rich caramel aroma and a smooth creamy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Caramel dip is made by caramelizing sugar at about 170 °C.
The classic recipe includes butter, which gives the sauce its silky mouthfeel.
In the United States the sauce is commonly used as a topping for fast‑food ice cream.
There is a salted caramel version that adds a subtle salty note.
Caramel dip can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 months.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The sugar in the dip provides quick glucose, which can be useful during intense physical activity.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Cream and butter are sources of calcium, important for bone health.

items.title: Vitamin A
items.content: Cream is rich in vitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk allergy should avoid the product.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Butter adds saturated fats, which should be limited in cardiovascular disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drizzle the caramel dip over ice cream, pancakes, waffles, yogurt, fruit salads, or stir into coffee for a sweet twist. Warm the sauce slightly in the microwave if a thinner consistency is desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator in a tightly sealed jar. Warm gently before use if the dip thickens. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or changes color.

content.title: About
content.content: A chocolate waffle is a light, crisp batter infused with rich cocoa and topped with melted chocolate. It is commonly served in fast‑food outlets and restaurants as a quick dessert or snack. The waffle is made from flour, eggs, milk, sugar and leavening, with chocolate added to the batter or as a glaze.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Waffles originated in medieval Europe as a way to quickly bake bread without a long oven time.
The first chocolate waffle recipe was published in the United States in the early 20th century.
Waffles are often used as a base for "waffle sandwiches" with ice cream, fruit, and whipped cream.
There are over 200 waffle shapes—from classic squares to heart‑shaped and star‑shaped molds.
Waffles stay crisp for up to a week when stored in an airtight container.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The carbohydrates provide quick glucose for active lifestyles.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Flour and cocoa powder are good sources of iron, essential for hemoglobin formation.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa supplies flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calcium from dairy
items.content: Milk in the batter adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and whole‑grain flour provide B1, B2 and B6 vitamins, supporting the nervous system.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Chocolate waffles often contain a lot of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional waffles are made with wheat flour, which may be problematic for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Trans‑fat content
items.content: Cooking in oils high in trans fats can increase cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A single serving can contain 300–500 kcal, so moderation is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the chocolate waffle warm, drizzle extra chocolate glaze, dust with powdered sugar, or top with fresh berries and whipped cream. It can also be used as a base for savory sandwiches with ham, cheese, or egg.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep waffles in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate or freeze them, reheating in a toaster before serving.
